articleTitle: A Novel Solar Power Interval Prediction Based on Combined Multiple Quantile Regression Models
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the stochastic nature of solar power, this paper proposes an interval forecasting model designed to enhance the accuracy of solar power predictions and improve the stability of power infrastructure. The model integrates multiple quantile regression approaches to overcome the limitations of traditional quantile regression, which typically relies solely on a single quantile loss function. Key metrics, including Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP) and Prediction Interval Normalized Average Width (PINAW), are introduced into the optimization criteria and optimized using a particle swarm optimization algorithm. Additionally, the upper and lower bounds of the prediction intervals are derived by aggregating results from different models through upper and lower bound weights, which are continually updated based on model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other approaches in terms of generalization ability and robustness when tested on a real-world solar power dataset, highlighting its effectiveness and reliability.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Micro Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator for Breeze Power Generation Based on Evolutionary Taguchi Method
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper designs a low-speed micro permanent magnet synchronous generator (MPMSG) suitable for generating electricity in urban breeze environments, aiming to efficiently convert wind energy. A novel evolutionary Taguchi method (ETM) capable of rapidly and accurately achieving generator optimization is proposed. Firstly, the performance of the generator is analyzed using the finite element method, demonstrating its satisfactory performance. Considering the requirements of urban breeze environments, the ETM is employed to optimize the generator. The optimization range of the optimization factors is analyzed and determined utilizing the genetic algorithm. Then the multi-objective optimization of the generator is conducted by using the Taguchi method. Finally, the performance of the optimized model is analyzed, verifying the effectiveness of the optimization method.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Optimization Approach for PV-BESS Integration in Grid-Tied EV Charging System
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This study introduces a hybrid optimization approach for optimizing the integration of PV systems and BESS to grid-tied EV charging stations to improve grid performance and sustainability. The proposed hybrid GWO-SA uses Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithms to optimize the location and size of PV units simultaneously and BESS, addressing PV output variability, EV load uncertainty, and peak load management. The proposed method considers the optimization of multi-objectives, including power loss and peak load minimization, voltage profile enhancement, and maximizing renewable energy utilization to facilitate EV charging needs and enhance the overall integrated system performance. The proposed method is validated on the IEEE 33-bus system under different power penetration levels, EV charging loads, and BESS configurations. Results show a significant power loss reduction of up to 53 % and an improvement in voltage stability from 0.903 pu to 1 pu. Moreover, peak demand is effectively managed, which indicates that the proposed framework reduces the load burden on the main grid during high-demand events. The validation and the comparison of the proposed GWO-SA algorithm demonstrated that the EV charging in the daytime aligned with PV generation proved the most efficient, reducing reliance on grid supply and robust convergence, while optimal-sized BESS achieved an optimal balance between EV charging stance and distribution network performance.

articleTitle: Electrification of Bus Line Along Simplon Route, Italy: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The urgency in renewing vehicle fleet in use for Local Public Transport is given for turning the transportation system more sustainable than before. Actually, almost the totality of suburban bus lines outside metropolitan areas are served by conventional Diesel buses. The need in a shift of transportation sector also outside the great cities must therefore be pursued to carry benefits also to the population and territory served. This paper outlines an electrification proposal for two existing bus lines connecting Milan to the city of Gallarate. A revised bus route along the Simplon route is presented, with a detailed analysis regarding the performances and emissions of the solution proposed, and a new service timetable and bus charging scheduling at depots is derived.

articleTitle: Impact of BESS Prices on Renewable Energy Integrated Public EV Charging Stations: Feasibility Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Private charging is currently the most popular, but to support the EV market, public charging requires more attention. However, public chargers mainly rely on the national grid, risking instability and reduced profits. Integrating renewable energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in public stations can address these issues but requires careful sizing. This study examines the technical and economic impacts of BESS on public Electric Vehicle Charging Station (EVCS), assessing project feasibility and efficiency. Results show grid-connected EVCS is about five times more profitable (2.5 million vs. 500 thousand). While hybrid station remains unviable due to current technology, a 67% drop in BESS prices would make standalone configuration more attractive, shifting the most profitable BESS size from zero to larger setups.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Market Trading in Integrated Electric Power-Grid and Hydrogen-Grid Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: To achieve a carbon-neutral society, it is necessary to introduce more renewable-energy components and hydrogen (H2) produced using renewable energy. However, when H2 is actively produced through electrolysis does not necessarily coincide with the demand for H2, so an energy-management system that adjusts the supply and demand of electricity and H2 is needed. We propose a method for enabling the provision of a mechanism to promote cooperation among each business operator to improve overall key performance indices (KPI) and a mechanism for building consensus on overall KPI. We also developed a prototype simulator for an electricity- and Hi-distrlbution-management system including a function for trading in multiple markets.

articleTitle: Energy Simulation-Based Design Optimization for Residential Buildings Using EnergyPlus
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With the growing focus on buildings' energy efficiency and sustainability, it is critical to model the energy consumption of residential buildings accurately. This study focuses on using EnergyPlus, a powerful building energy simulation software, to conduct an in-depth analysis of the energy performance of a chosen residential building prototype. Accurate building models are constructed with detailed input of key information such as the buildings' geometry, envelope characteristics, HVAC system parameters, personnel activities, and indoor and outdoor climate conditions. Through simulation using EnergyPlus, the impacts of different design parameters and operational strategies on energy consumption can be studied, such as window materials, shading facilities on lighting and cooling or heating loads, and the association of ventilation system efficiency with indoor air quality and energy consumption. In this research, literature review has been done on why residential building energy consumption plays an important role, the significance of integrating building energy modeling tools with building design process, and why EnergyPlus is chosen as the simulation tool. A case study has been conducted to investigate how changing temperature set-point can impact the building's energy performance, hence demonstrating the significance of optimizing design factors, such as temperature set- point schedule to minimize building energy consumption.

articleTitle: Smart Charging for PEVs to Enhance Radial Distribution Network Performance with Placement of Multiple DGs
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Optimal charging strategies are the key solution for integrating Electric Vehicles (EVs) into the distribution network (DN) to prevent congestion and mismatched power demands. In this paper, the impact of different charging scenarios of EVs on the performance of the distribution network is analyzed in the first stage which aims to balance the grid load and minimize the active power losses and node voltage deviations. In the second stage, the reactive power set points of the Distributed Generators (DGs) are optimized to minimize active power losses and node voltage deviation in DN. A 33-node radial distribution network (RDN) is used for the study. Time-series power flow optimization results reveal that optimized reactive power support from DGs and adopting smart charging of EVs in vehicle-to-grid (V2G) mode can effectively minimize voltage violations, and ensure stable network operation despite increasing DGs and EV penetration.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance of High Concentrator Photovoltaic Systems with Passive Cooling
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This study investigates the effect of secondary optics in High Concentrator Photovoltaic (HCPV) systems and evaluates three different passive cooling techniques using ANSYS Fluent and 3D modelling. The analysis incorporates changes in fin configurations and lengths to optimize the thermal management of HCPV cells. Data obtained under varying operation conditions demonstrate that the integration of secondary optics marginally influences the cell's thermal and electrical performance. The effectiveness of the cooling is largely governed by the design and configuration of the heat sink, such as the use of short fins, long fins, or pyramid-shaped fins rather than the secondary optics themselves. The fins enhance heat dissipation by increasing the surface area for convective cooling at the back of the HCPV cell.

articleTitle: Spectral Clustering and Multi-Modal Stable Matching for Enhanced Management of Photovoltaic Stations and Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: As renewable energy sources like photovoltaic (PV) stations expand, efficient management and operation are becoming increasingly important for maintaining grid stability and optimizing resource allocation. In this paper, we introduce a novel framework that integrates spectral clustering and multi-modal stable matching to enhance the coordination of PV stations and Virtual Power Plants (VPPs). We begin by applying spectral clustering to group PV stations based on geographic locations and key weather conditions. Our custom-built similarity matrix for PV stations, combined with our theoretical insights, suggests that using fewer eigenvectors in spectral clustering not only reduces computation time but also improves clustering accuracy. This method ensures that each cluster of PV stations shares similar environmental conditions, allowing for more effective collective management. In the second stage, we utilize multi-modal stable matching to assign these PV clusters to VPPs. Unlike traditional stable matching, the multi-modal approach considers multiple factors, such as energy demand, geographic proximity, and VPP capacity, resulting in a more balanced and stable allocation. We validate our approach through experiments on both synthetic and real-world PV station data. The results demonstrate that our framework leads to more accurate grouping of PV stations, facilitating more effective decision-making across multiple criteria. This also enhances work offloading when tasks become intensive on certain nodes. Our work presents a promising solution for managing large-scale renewable energy resources in future power systems, improving both efficiency and stability.

articleTitle: Development of a Mathematical Model for the Corona Effect: Sinusoidal and Impulsive Components and Parametric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This work presents the development of a mathe-matical model for the corona effect in high voltage systems, integrating both sinusoidal and impulsive components. The model was developed from experimental measurements performed in a corona cage at the High Voltage Laboratory of the Universidad Politécnica Salesiana in Cuenca, Ecuador. Using an alternative partial discharge detection method, the research characterized the fundamental behavior of the corona effect, including its sinusoidal base morphology and distinctive pulse patterns in positive and negative half cycles. The proposed mathematical model incorporates environmental variables such as temperature and humidity, along with applied voltage, through parametric analysis. The model parameters were determined using digital fil-tering techniques, adaptive thresholding algorithms and multiple regression analysis, resulting in a set of equations that describe both the fundamental sinusoidal component and the stochastic nature of the corona pulses.

articleTitle: Determination of Patterns of Surface and Corona Discharges in Polymer Insulators Since 13.8 kV Up to 22 kV
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This document presents a description of the behavior of polymeric insulators when a controlled amount of voltage is introduced, along with this its definition is also presented. There have also been some field tests applying the necessary voltage for which have been created. A program has also been designed in the Matlab software to make a visual comparison of each of the discharges that have occurred during the technical tests, so that it can be differentiated between superficial partial discharges and corona discharges, following the main standard which is IEC 60270.

articleTitle: A Double Frequency Commutation Mechanical DC Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In this paper, a double frequency commutation mechanical DC circuit breaker (DFC-MDCCB) was proposed. The working principle of DFC-MDCCB was analyzed and the simulation of interrupting process was conducted. The simulation results show that two sets of capacitors and inductors in commutation branch can oscillate to generate multi frequency superimposed current which can extend the commutation time and decrease the overall rise rate of TIV.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Power Systems Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Effective fault identification and diagnosis are critical in modern power systems to ensure operational reliability and reduce economic losses. This research describes a novel approach that uses machine learning techniques, notably Ensemble models, to improve fault detection and classification in electrical networks. Several fault situations were generated using a complete MATLAB/Simulink simulation, which captured important voltage and current data. The study compares the performance of several machine learning techniques, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Ensemble approaches, to various input configurations. The results show that Ensemble models greatly enhance fault detection accuracy and robustness when compared to standard methods, indicating its promise for real world applications in smart grid technology. This study not only tackles the issues of fault management in increasingly complex power systems, but it also establishes a framework for future advances in machine learning applications for electrical infrastructure.

articleTitle: An Enhanced MOEA/D Algorithm for Optimal Charging of Electric Vehicle Populations Considering Traffic and Power Grid Factors
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper addresses traffic dynamics and power grid constraints by proposing an enhanced Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Decomposition (EMOEA/D) to optimize charging strategies of electric vehicle (EV) populations. Firstly, the proposed algorithm systematically decomposes the addressed multi-objective problem into scalar optimization tasks and evolves them by using MOEA/D. Further, to assist decision-makers in selecting the most suitable solution from the Pareto Optimal Set (POS), a knee-point based method is employed to effectively balance the objectives of minimizing charging time and reducing power grid cost. Extensive simulations on a 48-node traffic system and a modified IEEE 118-bus power system demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, highlighting its contribution to the sustainability and stability of integrated transportation and energy systems.

articleTitle: Safety and Security Sensors for Smart EV Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: City transport systems often struggle to cope with high volumes of traffic and become congested, despite the use of various traffic management strategies. The concentration of traffic around city centres results in pollution and poor urban air quality, although the increasing popularity of electric vehicles is helping ameliorate these effects. One reason for the growing momentum behind electric vehicles is the emergence of mobility operators such as car-sharing companies, who target users wishing to rent out vehicles on a short-term basis. There is currently rapid growth in one-way car-sharing, in which the vehicle can be dropped off at a different location from the pickup point. Crucially, one-way car-sharing gives the opportunity for travellers to utilize car-sharing in conjunction with other modes, such as public transport modes, for their journey, provided the requisite intermodal connections are present. This paper looks at how one-way electric vehicle car-sharing systems have the potential to become important components of future city transport systems. The future role of shared autonomous vehicles is also considered.

articleTitle: VPP Profitability Assessment: Development of Simulator with EV Charge/Discharge and Electricity Trading Functions in Japan
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This study develops a simulator to compute and assess the profitability of a virtual power plant (VPP) that would contribute to discussing the promising business model of VPP for Japan's electricity market. The simulator examines how VPP maximizes the use of distributed energy resources (DERs) and profit under the existing power system. We examine the impacts of EVs' charge/discharge operation and electricity market trading on VPP profitability, in which EV s are used for supply and demand adjustment that optimizes profit. The use of EV sand electricity market trading is expected to reduce electricity costs in VPP compared to the case that does not use them. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of increased solar PV penetration on profitability.

articleTitle: Optimization Configuration Strategy for the Electro-Hydrogen Coupling System Considering the Uncertainty of New Energy Output
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The uncertainty of renewable energy output can lead to over- or under-sizing of components such as energy storage and hydrogen production facilities in the electro-hydrogen system, affecting its stability and economic efficiency. To address this, this paper proposes an optimization configuration strategy for the electro-hydrogen coupling system considering the uncertainty of new energy output. Firstly, mathematical models for the components of the electro-hydrogen system are established. Next, the uncertainty of renewable energy output in the electro-hydrogen system is described based on the WGAN-GP model. Then, a bi-Ievel capacity configuration model for the electro-hydrogen system is proposed, with the upper level focusing on capacity optimization and the lower level on operational optimization. The differential evolution algorithm is used to solve the model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed configuration strategy is validated through a case study.

articleTitle: Static Analysis in the Planning of Adding Ocean Current Power Plant to the Nusa Penida Electrical System
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The demand for electricity in Indonesia will continue to increase even until 2020, including Nusa Penida. Nusa Penida currently uses diesel power plants as one of its leading suppliers. However, the Bali government is targeting the use of renewable energy in Nusa Penida by 2025. Additional renewable energy-based power plants are needed to reduce the use of diesel power plants. The potential that can be utilized is the ocean current power plant in the Toyapakeh Strait. Then, with the addition of the ocean current power plant, an analysis of the Nusa Penida electrical system is needed. The load flow simulation results show that the number of diesel power plants decreases with the addition of ocean current power plants. The load flow simulation occurs under both peak load and off-peak load conditions. In addition, the short circuit analysis also shows that there are no current values exceeding the established standards. That means the electrical system is safe and will not damage the components.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Prospects of Wind-Diesel Hybrid Power Systems to meet Commercial Loads of Qaisumah of SaudiArabia-A Pathway for Sustainable Energy Development
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Commercial/residential buildings of Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (K.S.A.) consume appreciable portion (10–40 percent) of energy generated. The aim of the current investigation includes assessment (technical & economical) of wind-diesel-hybrid power system (WDHPS) to fulfill electrical load requirement (620 MWh-annually) of a typical commercial-building at Qaisumah (Eastern Region, K.S.A.) through data analysis of wind-speed (long-term). Data analysis shows that long-term-monthly-average (LTMA) is between 3.5 and 4.6 meter per sec at height of 10m. The WDHPS simulated encompass different combinations of 100kW wind turbines (wind energy systems- WES) and diesel systems. The viability (techno-economic) of WDHS has been performed by use of HOMER software of NREL (HOMER-Energy). The simulation-outcomes point out that the wind fraction (with no load-rejection) is 39% for a WDHPS setup comprising of two-100kW wind turbine generator (WTG) together and 175kW diesel-generator. The cost of energy generation (COE) for this WDHPS is $0.167 per-kWh. Notably, the 39% wind fraction leads to a decrease in emissions of carbon by 158 tons annually. Particular focus is given to the impact of wind fraction on various factors, including energy production, COE, excess-energy, savings in fuel, and the reduction in emissions of carbon in comparison to a diesel-only scenario.

articleTitle: A Smart Peak-Demand Curtailment Strategy for Residential Communities with Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has created significant challenges and opportunities in grid management. This study focuses on reducing peak load on the grid by reducing the peak demand of a community of residences having EVs. To implement this strategy practically, a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)-based EV charging model is proposed, tailored to curtail the peak demands. This strategy integrates real-world constraints such as EV charging behaviours and residential demand patterns to optimize energy distribution during peak periods. By dynamically adjusting charging and discharging schedules and enabling effective demand-side management, the PSO model minimizes stress on the grid and improves energy efficiency. The simulation results from a case with 5, 000 residences and 1, 000 EVs have shown a total 9.6% peak reduction, demonstrating the potential of the proposed method in supporting the grid while addressing user convenience.

articleTitle: An Overview of Practical Impact When Implementing Energy Savings Solutions on Quality of Electrical Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In the race to achieve sustainability goals, decarbonization, reduce CO2 emission and other environmental, social and governance (ESG)‘s requirements and compliances, many businesses turn to implementing energy savings solutions and installing renewable energies to meet the criteria. Although these steps are considered low hanging fruits which are relatively easy to implement to achieve substantial results, their impact on the quality of electrical power system is often overlooked. This ‘blind spot’ cannot be neglected because all those equipment consists of power electronics devices and switches that are used for control or convert power from ac-to-dc and vice-versa. This power conversion technology is known to have generated harmonics and pollute the electrical network. This paper expounds on the practical impact of implementing the common energy savings solutions, focusing on variable speed drives, power factor correction capacitor bank, and LED lightings, on the quality of electrical power system. This paper also presents the mitigation solutions to overcome their impact, and the common pitfalls of neglecting them.

articleTitle: Enhancing Day-ahead PV Power Forecast Accuracy with an Improved Informer Model Using AdaBelief Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Renewable Energy sources (REs) have recently emerged as crucial elements in the sustainable development of human society. Therefore, an accurate REs power generation forecast is considered to be a key countermeasure to maintain the stability and reliability of the grid. Recently, advanced Transformer-based models have gained more and more attention from researchers, especially in the field of time-series forecasting. This paper proposed an Informer model improved with AdaBelief optimizer for day-ahead PV power forecast. Replacing the conventional self-attention with ProbSpare self-attention technique increases the training efficiency and forecasting accuracy and significantly reduces the training period compared to the basic Transformer. Moreover, the AdaBelief, can both bear faster convergence and effective generalization, further enhancing the precision of the proposed model. A 5-minute multivariate dataset is employed for accessing the forecasting performance of the proposed model and demonstrates the enhancement of each module to the forecasting efficiency.

articleTitle: An Energy-Saving Path Planning Method for Autonomous Trucks in Underground Mining Areas
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With the advancement of green mining initiatives, the high energy consumption and emissions in underground mining transportation have become critical challenges restricting sustainable development in the industry. To optimize energy use and support green transitions in mining operations, this study proposes an energy-saving path planning method based on an improved Lagrangian relaxation algorithm. The method optimizes transportation cost, time, and energy-saving objectives, enhancing the efficiency of multi-trucks collaborative operations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces energy consumption in complex multi-trucks transportation scenarios, achieving an average energy-saving rate of 6.12%, and outperforms traditional solvers such as CPLEX and Gurobi in computational efficiency and planning performance. These findings provide essential theoretical support and practical guidance for advancing energy savings and green energy transitions in mining transportation.

articleTitle: Dynamic Demand Optimization in Grids with Distributed Solar Photovoltaic and Vehicle-to-Grid Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles presents both opportunities and challenges for the sustainable operation of electric grids. While electric vehicles help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and dependence on fossil fuels, their integration intro-duces complexities such as demand fluctuations, grid asset stress, and power quality issues. This paper focuses on dynamic demand optimization in electric grids by incorporating distributed solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology. By developing an optimization framework that accounts for solar PV output, electric vehicle state of charge (SOC), and grid demand, this study aims to enhance grid flexibility and miti-gate peak demand impacts. The proposed framework improves grid efficiency by synchronizing PEV charging with solar PV generation and leveraging V2G technology for peak shaving.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Heat Transfer of the Airflow in a Circular Tube
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of using new twisted tape (TT) inserts with rings on the Nusselt number (Nu) and friction factor (f) for heat exchangers and air intercoolers. The analysis compares the effects of air and water as cooling fluids. The experimental setup is used to obtain experimental data needed for Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) validation. Then, the CFD model is utilized to predict the impact of using the new TT insert with rings compared to the conventional TT without rings under various conditions, which cannot be attained by the experimental facilities at the laboratory scale. The results show that the proposed TT insert with rings significantly enhances heat transfer efficiency while maintaining acceptable pressure drops. The findings suggest that incorporating TT with rings can optimize heat transfer performance in various heating and cooling applications. The experimental results show that adding the rings to the TT improves the heat transfer characteristics compared with the TT without rings, especially at larger TT pitch distances. Further, the experimental results demonstrate that the Nu values when using the TT inserts with rings significantly increase by up to 25% more than smooth pipes at low air velocities with larger pitch distances and by about 43 % at higher velocities with smaller pitch distances. However, this increase in heat transfer also leads to a rise in the friction factor, which increases by up to four times at low velocities and larger pitch distances and up to seven times higher at greater velocities and smaller pitch distances.

articleTitle: Dynamic Control of Microgrids with Battery Energy Storage Systems: Grid-Forming and Grid-Following Modes with Adaptive Disconnection Criteria
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs), such as photovoltaic (PV) systems, into modern power grids has accelerated the adoption of microgrid technology, enhancing grid flexibility and resilience. However, the intermittent nature of RESs presents significant challenges to microgrid stability, especially during grid disturbances. To address these challenges, battery energy storage systems (BESS) have become essential for microgrid operations, enabling dynamic control of voltage and frequency. This paper proposes a novel control strategy for microgrids that leverages a BESS capable of seamlessly transitioning between grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM) modes. These transitions are governed by real-time monitoring of key parameters: voltage, frequency, phase difference, and active power. It incorporates an adaptive disconnection mechanism that dynamically adjusts threshold values for parameter deviations, ensuring a coordinated and robust response. Notably, the microgrid transitions to islanded mode and disconnects from the main grid with the BESS shifts to grid-forming mode only when the rate of change of all monitored parameters simultaneously exceeds their respective thresholds. This coordinated approach ensures reliable decision-making while minimizing unnecessary disconnections. Simulation results validate the proposed strategy, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing microgrid resilience, reducing false positives, and ensuring smooth transitions between grid-connected and islanded modes. The case study demonstrate the proposed model's superior fault detection and recovery capabilities over traditional fixed threshold strategies. This research provides a robust solution to improve microgrid stability and reliability, addressing the complexities associated with the increasing penetration of RESs.

articleTitle: Arduino Controlled Leading-Edge Phase Dimming for Lighting Control System
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper investigates LED bulb dimming technology, specifically focusing on leading-edge phase control methodology. A hardware circuit was designed and implemented to evaluate the performance of this technique. The circuit consists of a zero-crossing TRIAC dimmer, an Arduino Nano microcontroller, a dimmable LED bulb as the load, and a TRIAC optocoupler to generate control signals. The testing and analysis aim to assess the performance and cost-effectiveness of leading-edge dimming compared to trailing-edge dimming in lighting applications.

articleTitle: Rat Swarm Versus Particle Swarm Intelligent Optimization Algorithms for Maximum Power Point Tracking in Designing Energy-Efficient Solar Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Recently, Photovoltaic (PV) devices generate electricity directly from sunlight, so their integration into urban infrastructure will not only generate energy but also reduce carbon emissions. Due to those advantages, solar energy plays a crucial role in developing smart cities. However, the efficiency of PV systems is heavily dependent on their ability to operate at the Maximum Power Point (MPP), which represents the bias potential at which the solar cell outputs the maximum net power. This paper employs an intelligent optimization algorithm, RAT Swarm, to find the optimal voltage the PV system can operate to produce maximum power. MATLAB software is used to model and simulate the system using the Rate Swarm algorithm. The simulation results show that the RAT based MPPT has been capable of achieving the capability to precisely track the maximum power point and to maximize the power output of the PV system. Furthermore, the same software is employed to implement and simulate the well-known particle swarm optimization algorithm for comparison. Convergence speed, trading accuracy as well as the stability of power, voltage and current under both uniform and time varying irradiance conditions are also considered in the comparison. Comparative evaluation indicates that RSO is a viable option for PSO owing to faster convergence. Nevertheless, the stability of RSO and the absence of an oscillation in the power output have to be investigated. These improvements would enable RSO to become optimally effective, achieving fast convergence and stable output power for energy capture from PV systems.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Transformers for Voltage Perception and Control in Low Voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With the rapid development of distributed energy resources and electric vehicles, the operational complexity of distribution networks, particularly low-voltage distribution networks (LVDNs), has significantly increased. Due to limited observability, high stochastic load variations, and complex network topologies, achieving real-time voltage situational awareness and dynamic control in LVDNs remains a major challenge. Traditional methods struggle to quickly converge and provide comprehensive and accurate situational awareness under such conditions. This paper proposes a Transformer and SAC-based method for voltage situational awareness and control in LVDNs. The Transformer network dynamically captures the spatiotemporal dependencies of voltage states, enhancing the perception and regulation of critical nodes, while the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm ensures adaptive voltage control in stochastic environments, improving real-time responsiveness and accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits strong robustness and fast convergence across various complex LVDN scenarios, effectively capturing voltage situational changes and significantly reducing voltage fluctuations and violation risks.

articleTitle: Distributed Energy Management in a Hybrid Cloud Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an IoT EDGE-cloud communication framework using the MQTT messaging protocol, designed to serve as the foundation for a future smart energy management system. A bidirectional communication channel is implemented between an IoT EDGE device and the cloud to ensure continuous data transfer. The paper details the technical challenges encountered during development and the corresponding solutions, along with the potential areas for future work. The system is primarily coded in Python, leveraging tools such as Command Prompt and Visual Studio Code. Additionally, the implementation integrates various cloud services, including AWS IoT Core, Lambda, DynamoDB, Timestream, EC2, and CloudWatch, which are crucial to the development and operational performance of communication channel. The proposed solution is applicable in real-world scenarios, paving the way for advancements in energy technology such as peer-to-peer energy trading.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study of Partial Energy Harvesting by Solar Cages for Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The demand for energy is ever-increasing around the world whereas the sources are limited. The study focuses on renewable energy harvesting partially and the remaining energy in terms of illuminations intensity available for nature or food production. To this end, miniature solar cages have been modelled and built for the study. A solar cage has solar panels of a specific area with a carrying structure for measurement; the panels are made of a series of photovoltaic, PV, cells soldered by a specific solder. The initial study includes a custom made 3-panel solar cage where the geometric parameter of the structure was constant. In the next stage, a custom made 5-panel solar cage has been built where the structure is flexible in terms of height adjustment. The power generation by the cage and illumination intensity available inside the cage have been measured for wide weather variation and over several days. The quantitative outcomes show a large variation of illumination intensity inside the cages over a day. The remaining energy inside can be used as an indicator of sustainability of a biological system to thrive.

articleTitle: Consumer Phase Identification of LVDNs with Green Energy Based on Weighted Least Squares Driven by Improved PSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: To improve the accuracy of consumer phase intelligent identification (CPII) in low-voltage distribution networks, this paper proposes a novel phase identification method based on Weighted Least Squares driven by improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. Firstly, a data screening scheme is introduced to remove abnormal data. Then, the individual update scheme of the PSO algorithm is improved. Subsequently, a weighted least squares method driven by the improved PSO algorithm is designed for CPII to reduce the impact of grey data. Finally, simulations are conducted on an actual low-voltage distribution network topology, and the results show that the proposed method enhances identification accuracy.

articleTitle: Examining Rooftop Solar Power with Integrated Storage Systems under Current Vietnam Pricing Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With growing concerns about climate change, energy security, and rising electricity costs, a rooftop solar system with storage offers a compelling solution for both residential and commercial consumers. Over the past decade, Vietnam has consistently implemented a series of mechanisms aimed at determining renewable energy pricing and supporting developers due to the high costs of self-investment and the imperative for profitable subsidies. The study examines a rooftop solar system with battery energy storage for a banking office building. By employing the self-consumption method, the system's installed capacity is optimized for economic efficiency. This smart investment solution not only reduces electricity costs for the building but also minimizes reliance on the grid, leading to reduced losses for utilities and a decreased carbon footprint. Furthermore, it encourages sustainable practices and demonstrates social responsibility by reducing the environmental impact of electricity generation.

articleTitle: A Constant-Power Bidirectional Double-Sided LCC Inductive Wireless Power Transfer Battery Charger with Triple-Phase-Shift Optimal Efficiency Control
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper proposes a constant-power (CP) double-sided inductor-capacitor-capacitor (DS-LCC) bidirectional wireless power transfer battery charger. Specifically, this charger adopts a DS-LCC compensation network and an active rectifier on the secondary side without involving any DC-DC converter(s) or switch-controlled capacitor(s). On this basis, the triple-phase-shift (TPS) modulation method is introduced in the charger to enable all devices to achieve soft switching. In addition, a novel Constant Power Optimal Efficiency Control (CPOEC) strategy is proposed, which utilizes a lookup table obtained from the offline optimization method to ensure the charger can achieve constant output power and optimal efficiency simultaneously. The feasibility of the proposed CP charger has been verified through simulation, with an efficiency range of 90.67% to 92.41%, which is excellent among state-of-the-art CP wireless chargers.

articleTitle: Tripping Fault Analysis Caused by Inaccurate Measurement of Optical CT in ±800 kV UHVDC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The ultra-high voltage direct current (UHVDC) power transmission systems usually transmit very large amounts of powers, their stability and reliability are of vital importance to the large power grid. This paper analyses a tripping fault caused by the inaccurate measurement of optical current transformer (OCT) in Shaanbei-Wuhan ± 800kV UHVDC transmission system. Combined with theoretical analysis and in-plant testing of the optical CT, a comprehensive understanding of the factors contributing to the fault is achieved. It reveals that optical CT measurement anomalies were significant contributors to the tripping fault. Validation results illustrate the effectiveness in measuring very fast impulse current accurately by adding automatic reset logic in the software programme of OCT. This study provides a guarantee and foundation for the stable operation of UHVDC transmission systems.

articleTitle: Extending Energy Flexibility for Demand Response Hybrid Utility Systems in the food Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Electrification, particularly in highly renewable grids, is not seen as viable by industry due to price volatility, but this can be addressed through demand response. However, biochemical industries such as food cannot easily manipulate their production operations to engage in demand response. Hybrid biomass-electric systems allow for engaging in demand response, while providing uninterrupted heat supply. In grids with high percentage of renewables, there can be frequent periods of low price and also high price volatility. Technologies can be implemented in utility systems to take advantage of this and provide mitigation against high prices. This work examined the cost-effectiveness of battery storage, heat pumps and PV arrays being integrated into hybrid system being applied to the food industry in New Zealand. Simulations were used to explore different system designs and operating strategies, determining the most economical options to extend the hybrid utility system. Heat pumps were found to be the most cost-effective, reducing costs by up to 3.2 %, with batteries not being economical due to poor performance relative to cost. Operating strategies across both heat pumps and batteries were found to have negligible impacts, with capacity sizing appearing far more significant of a choice. PV arrays proved to be most impactful during periods of high prices, with fuel cost reductions of up to 0.7 %, and thus should be paired with heat pumps for a holistic solution.

articleTitle: Productive Efficiency and Renewable Power Generation in the US Electricity Companies
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This study measures the productive efficiency of 72 US electric power companies from 2013 to 2022 using a meta-frontier analysis of the data envelopment analysis (DEA) intermediate approach. The intermediate approach incorporates features of radial and non-radial DEA models. We classify the electric power companies according to the ratio of renewable power generation to total generation and examine differences in the efficiency levels among the groups. We find that companies with medium levels of renewable power generation ratios exhibit higher productive efficiency. From the results, this study discusses policy implications to promote balanced adoption of renewable power that can enhance the productive efficiency of companies.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Diagnosis and Analysis Technology of Main Equipment in Distribution Network Based on Data Value Mining Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With the continuous strengthening of power grid supervision, the traditional extensive power equipment asset management mode has some deficiencies. It is necessary to change the management concept, innovate the asset management mode, introduce scientific decision-making, and optimize the management strategy. Therefore, based on the data value mining technology, this paper constructs the fault diagnosis and analysis technology of the main equipment of the distribution network, which can provide reference and reference for the power grid enterprises to effectively manage the equipment failure situation and ensure the normal and safe operation of the equipment.

articleTitle: Smart DC Nanogrid Control for Rural Electrification
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This research presents the design and implementation of a smart control system for DC nanogrids aimed at rural electrification. The system integrates renewable energy sources like solar power with advanced control strategies to optimize power distribution and maintain stability under varying conditions, thus addressing the unique challenges of providing reliable energy to remote areas. Findings from simulations demonstrate the system's effectiveness in managing energy flow, significantly reducing energy losses and maintaining a steady power supply. This work contributes to sustainable electrification solutions by enhancing energy accessibility, which can lead to improved living standards and economic growth in isolated communities. The implications of these advancements underscore the system's potential to facilitate cost-effective, environmentally friendly power alternatives, supporting the larger goal of bridging the energy access gap in rural regions.

articleTitle: A Multi-Modal Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In the context of widespread solar energy deployment, accurate prediction of photovoltaic power generation is crucial to ensure safe and stable operation of power systems. Extracting spatiotemporal features from ground-based sky images can significantly improve the accuracy of ultra-short-term photovoltaic power forecasting. Although previous studies have relied heavily on multimodal data for power forecasting, multimodal datasets are usually small and may not be sufficient to fully train complex models, resulting in poor model performance. Directly processing multimodal data requires learning the relationship between multiple modalities simultaneously, which increases training complexity. In this paper, an innovative learning strategy is proposed to construct a more generalized deep learning model by pre-training the sky image processing module and the time series data processing module. Specifically, this paper first uses a single-modal dataset to train the image processing module and the time series reasoning module separately, and then fuses them into a multimodal framework to achieve prediction through interactive attention mechanism and adaptive cross-modal fusion. The results show that the components learned through single-modal training can effectively collaborate, allowing the multimodal framework to achieve competitive results after fine-tuning.

articleTitle: Decentralized Microgrid Energy Management: A Cooperative Game Approach for Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This article introduces an innovative platform for microgrids (MGs) that enables active energy trading both with the main power grid and directly among MGs. By facilitating Peer-to-Peer (P2P) energy trading, the proposed platform ensures mutually beneficial outcomes, particularly in the presence of advanced energy resources such as Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs) and Demand Response Programs (DRPs). From the perspective of power systems, P2P energy trading enhances local energy balancing and promotes self-sufficiency within MG networks. Unlike traditional noncooperative game models, where participants act independently, this study adopts a cooperative game approach that aligns with the autonomous and self-interested nature of MGs. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness of the platform, demonstrating that MGs can engage in energy trading while achieving economic benefits. Fur-thermore, the platform determines optimal pricing and energy trading volumes, ensuring that participants gain measurable eco-nomic advantages in the P2P market. Additionally, technologies such as BESSs and DRPs significantly enhance energy sharing among MGs, thereby improving overall system efficiency and sustainability.

articleTitle: Advantages of Smart EV Charging for Power Loss Reduction in Low-Voltage Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In the context of rising electricity consumption, the widespread adoption of electric vehicles and massive de-ployment of distributed generation, improving energy efficiency and minimizing power losses in low-voltage grids are essential challenges for the electric power industry. This study evaluates the performance of a residential distribution network under varying penetration levels of electric vehicles and photovoltaic generation in different combinations. The analysis highlights the effectiveness of grid-aware charging of electric vehicles in minimizing power losses compared to uncontrolled charging. The findings provide insights for grid planning and infrastructural investment prioritization.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of STATCOM, SVC, TCSC, and UPFC for Power Flow Balance and Efficiency of Parallel Distribution Lines
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Efficient power delivery and reliable system operation are critical in modern electrical distribution networks. The 69 kV parallel distribution line of the Cagayan de Oro Power Distribution System faces challenges such as high losses, congestion, and fluctuating reliability due to increasing load demand and distributed generation (DG) integration. Flexible AC Transmission System (FACTS) devices, including Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM), Static VAR Compensator (SVC), Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC), and Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC), offer technological solutions to optimize power flow, improve system reliability, and enhance overall efficiency. This paper presents a comparative analysis of the effects of these FACTS devices on the operational performance of the 69 kV parallel distribution line. Using MATLAB for simulation, the study evaluates the devices' impact on critical performance parameters, including power flow optimization, transmission efficiency, and system reliability under varied loading conditions. Results indicate that while all FACTS devices enhance system performance, UPFC demonstrates the most comprehensive improvement in terms of reducing line losses, balancing power flow, and ensuring operational reliability. This comparative analysis provides insights into selecting the most appropriate FACTS for future implementation in Cagayan de Oro Distribution System and as well as other distribution networks facing similar challenges.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Based on GMM Weather Classification and BiLSTM-ATTENTION
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The high integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems introduces significant grid instability and randomness to distribution networks. Understanding PV power output is crucial for improving grid stability. To address this, this paper proposes a hybrid PV power forecasting model based on GMM (Gaussian Mixture Model) weather classification. Firstly, PV generation data is normalized and analyzed for correlations. The GMM clustering algorithm is then used to classify the data into three weather types: sunny, rainy, and cloudy. Next, a BiLSTM-Attention neural network is constructed by integrating BiLSTM (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) with an attention mechanism to enhance prediction. Finally, case study comparisons demonstrate that the proposed model can effectively capture local features with high prediction variability under different weather conditions, significantly improving both the accuracy and stability of PV power forecasting.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Thermo-Electrical Performance of Low-Concentrator Photovoltaic Module using Design of Experiments
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: A promising approach to enhance the power output of photovoltaic (PV) modules is through low-concentration photovoltaic (LCPV) systems. However, increased solar radiation in these systems elevates temperatures, significantly reducing electrical efficiency. This study addresses the issue by proposing an optimized converging cooling channel attached to the rear of monocrystalline LCPV modules, with a variable height at the channel outlet. Using design of experiments (DOE) approach, six input factors including cooling fluid velocity (Vin), fluid temperature (Tin), outlet channel height (Hout), solar concentration ratio (CR), solar irradiance (G), and wind speed (Vw) are investigated for their effects on electrical and thermal efficiency. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model, simulated with ANSYS Fluent, is used to evaluate performance. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) identifies significant factors and interactions, while regression models predict system efficiencies. The results indicate that solar irradiance, CR, and Tin strongly affect electrical efficiency, whereas Vin, Vw, and Hout mainly influence thermal efficiency. The optimized design yields an electrical efficiency of 15.4% and a thermal efficiency of 68.1 % under optimal conditions: Yin = 0.009 m/s, Tin = 298.15 K, Vw = 0 m/s, G = 1100 W/m2, CR = 3 suns, and Hout = 3 mm.

articleTitle: Modeling Industry Power Systems with Integrated Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This paper presents modelling and integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) using a software such as Electrical Transient Analyzer Program (ETAP) to improve the efficiency of the Industry Power System and save cost by reducing power supply from the grid. The DERs used in this work are solar photovoltaic (PV) system, battery energy storage system (BESS) and electric vehicle (EV) charger. Each DERs components were further studied in this work to ensure efficiency compatibility and reduce power loss when interacting with the power system. A bi-directional rectifier used to support the interaction by enabling the flow of AC and DC power between the power system and the DERs component. Multiple scenarios of different load variations were performed to observe the efficiency and reliability of the DERs components. The results from these scenarios were analyzed and further studied to form a peak shaving curve and an estimated economic cost of this work.

articleTitle: Wind Power Prediction Based on SSA-SVM
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the wind power prediction accuracy is not high due to wind volatility and randomness, a prediction model based on sparrow search algorithm (SSA) and support vector machine (SVM) was designed. Firstly, the method based on Thompson tau and quartile was used to identify and process the abnormal data of wind speed and wind power. Then, SSA was used to optimize the penalty coefficient and the kernel parameter of SVM, and SSA-SVM prediction model was constructed. Through the experimental simulation analysis of the measured data from a wind farm in China, it is proved that SSA-SVM prediction model is effective, and the prediction accuracy of the proposed model is improved compared with the prediction model based on SVM.

articleTitle: Weather-Driven Priority Charging for Battery Storage Systems in Hybrid Renewable Energy Grids
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy into the power grid is often hindered by its fragmented infrastructure, leading to inefficient utilization due to the variability of energy production and its reliance on weather conditions. Battery storage systems, while essential for stabilizing energy supply, face challenges like suboptimal energy distribution, accelerating battery degradation, and reducing operational efficiency. This paper presents a novel solution to these challenges by developing a large-scale, interconnected renewable energy network that optimizes energy storage and distribution. The proposed system includes strategically placed battery storage facilities that stabilize energy production by compensating for fluctuations in renewable output. A priority charging algorithm, informed by real-time weather forecasting and load monitoring, ensures that the most suitable battery systems are charged under varying conditions. Within each storage facility, a secondary priority charging algorithm minimizes battery degradation by ranking batteries based on critical parameters such as state of health (SoH) and state of charge (SoC) and deciding which to charge. This comprehensive approach enhances the efficiency and longevity of battery storage systems, offering a more reliable and resilient renewable energy infrastructure.

articleTitle: Optimizing Generation Expansion Planning Through Carbon Pricing for Sustainable Energy Transition in Bangka Island
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This study examines the role of carbon pricing mechanisms in optimizing Generation Expansion Planning (GEP) for Bangka Island, a key region within Indonesia's energy and climate framework, which houses 79% of the Bangka Belitung Province's population. Using a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) approach, the GEP model evaluates economic and environmental impacts under three scenarios—Business-as-Usual (BAU), Emission Trading System (ETS), and Carbon Tax (CT)—spanning the period from 2023 to 2050. The BAU scenario projects a significant increase in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions, rising from 362,160 tCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in 2023 to 1,746,459 tCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by 2050, with fossil fuels continuing to dominate the energy mix and renewable energy adoption remaining minimal. Total costs steadily increase to USD 116.8 million, underscoring the risks associated with inaction on climate policies. In contrast, the ETS scenario achieves a renewable energy share surpassing the 30.97% target for 2050, reducing emissions to 1,501,650 tCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, with total costs reaching USD 139.1 million by 2050. The CT scenario demonstrates further emissions reductions, lowering emissions to 1,474,163 tCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by implementing progressively rising carbon prices, starting at USD 2/tCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in 2023 and reaching USD 90/tCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in 2048. However, this scenario incurs the highest total cost of USD 262.4 million by 2050, reflecting the financial challenges of transitioning to low-carbon technologies. These findings highlight the complementary strengths of ETS and CT in balancing economic efficiency and environmental sustainability. The study provides actionable insights for policymakers, supporting Indonesia's efforts to exceed its Paris Agreement commitments and achieve Net Zero Emission (NZE) targets by 2060 or earlier.

articleTitle: Integrating Renewables: Insights from Global Pumped Hydro Storage Case Studies
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy (RE) sources, such as solar and wind, into the power grid presents unique challenges to grid stability and reliability due to their intermittent and variable nature. The paper examines the integration of intermittent renewable energy sources (IRES) with pumped hydro storage (PHS) to enhance grid stability and reliability. Through a detailed analysis of multiple case studie including Japan's advanced synchronous PHS, the Huanghe Hydropower Golmud Solar Park in China, and solar-PHS integration efforts in Cyprus and the Faroe Islands key metrics such as energy storage efficiency, capacity factors, and curtailment rates were evaluated. The findings reveal that Japan and China exemplify successful models, demonstrating high energy storage efficiency and minimal curtailment rates, thereby achieving significant carbon emissions reductions and robust grid stability. Conversely, Cyprus faced challenges due to lower capacity and efficiency in its PHS facilities, highlighting barriers to effective integration. The paper discusses the broader implications for renewable energy deployment, emphasizing the necessity for supportive policies, technological innovations, and investments in infrastructure. Recommendations for future research areas, including advancements in energy storage technologies and grid modernization efforts, are also presented. This study underscores the vital role of IRES and PHS integration in promoting sustainable power systems and achieving energy transition goals.

articleTitle: Driving Towards Sustainability: V2G Technology and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: As the number of renewable energy sources connected to the grid and electricity demand grows, the electricity system faces unprecedented stability challenges as it responds to carbon neutrality policies. Vehicle-to-grid (V2G), as an emerging technology, can alleviate the stability problems caused by the peak-valley effect of the grid. This study dynamically analyzes the economic and environmental benefits of V2G applications in the context of increasing electric vehicle (EV) ownership, considering costs associated with battery charging, degradation, investment, and operation and maintenance. The results show that by 2060, the daily peak shaving potential of V2G will reach 76.87 TWh, potentially avoiding approximately 69.32 million tons (Mt) of carbon emissions. With advances in battery technology, the levelized cost of storage (LCOS) for V2G is projected to decrease to 0.39 CNY.kWh-1 by 2060, increasing the net present value (NPV) per vehicle to 163.13 thousand CNY, with carbon emission reductions reaching 0.37 Mt. These results indicate that V2G has great potential for application in future energy systems and can bring significant economic and environmental benefits.

articleTitle: A Software Sensor-Based Protection Against Cyber-Physical Attacks in Power Systems with High Penetration of DERs
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Towards the global goal of the decarbonization, more and more renewable distributed energy resources (DERs) are integrating into the power system. These IoT devices are numerous and controlled by commercial third parties, which changes the communication mode and lacks sufficient security standards and protections. They might be compromised ma-liciously and become the entrance to attack the distributed renewable power generation systems, which could cause chaos of the electrical markets and even large scale blackouts across the power grid. In this paper, considering the characteristics of the DERs, we propose a three tier protection framework including device layer, network layer and application layer to protect the distributed renewable power generation system from the cyber-physical threats and achieve its self-immunity. Particularly, we propose the software sensor method on the device layer based on the techniques of system identification and Kalman filter to accurately estimate the system states and thus protect the system from attacks.

articleTitle: Low-Voltage Consumer Phase Identification Method Based on Randomised Domain Search with Feature Constraints
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Low-voltage distribution networks (LVDNs) are crucial for maintaining user satisfaction, yet their vast and dynamic nature complicates the accurate monitoring of phase sequence information, leading to issues such as line losses and phase imbalances. Current phase identification methods, including manual inspections and signal-based techniques, are inefficient and vulnerable to external disturbances. This paper proposes a novel methodology combining Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) for dimensionality reduction with an enhanced CLARAN-Medoids clustering algorithm. UMAP captures the intrinsic nonlinear relationships in voltage time-series data, while CLARAN-Medoids integrates a randomized neighborhood search and Cannot-link constraints to enhance clustering robustness against noise and phase misalignment. Experimental results from three transformer districts in Southern China demonstrate the superior performance of our approach, with accuracy improvements of up to 10.9% compared to traditional methods. This research provides a reliable solution for precise phase sequence identification in LVDNs, with potential applications in advanced metering infrastructure and dynamic grid management.

articleTitle: Robust Fault Detection System for Batteries in Renewable Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Battery Energy Storage systems play a significant role in renewable energy grids, where fault detection is critical to ensuring reliability, safety, and optimal performance. Existing methods for fault detection, which are model-based Kalman filters and data-driven signal processing techniques, could be effective but face limitations in detecting slight issues or early signs of deterioration. This paper presents a novel hybrid approach to real-time fault detection which integrates signal processing techniques with Kalman filter-based state estimation. The proposed model is designed to detect faults and predict degradation trends, thereby enhancing the overall health mon-itoring of battery systems. This detailed methodology covers signal acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, Kalman filter design, and residual analysis. Kalman filter predicts system state and performs residual analysis to identify faults. Post-Kalman filter signal processing methods like wavelet transforms are used to analyze the residuals and detect fault-specific patterns, allowing for precise fault classification, including overcharging and short circuits. This hybrid approach combines the strengths of real-time state estimation and signal processing to advance real-time battery health monitoring, which results in a robust, scalable solution for fault detection in battery Storage Systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Modelling and Simulation of Small Wind Turbine System Using MATLAB/Simulink Based on Various Power Coefficient Models in Kupang-Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: With the rapid depletion of fossil fuels that cause environmental impact such as climate change while the need for energy, especially electricity, is increasing in demand, the use of renewable energy must be immediately executed. One of the types available in most parts of the world is wind energy. In Indonesia, this energy can be implemented in Kupang, Nusa Tenggara Timur due to its high potential in which in contrast, has faced electricity crisis and frequent blackouts. Thus, this research aims to models and compares small wind turbines based on existing power coefficient mathematical approaches which are polynomial, sinusoidal, and exponential using MATLAB/Simulink. The result of this study is based on the selected model, which is the Ovando et al. model with a coefficient of 0.4513. This model produced power in the range of 9000–16000 W under the assumption of periodic wind speeds of 50–60 km/h. The calculations were based on pre-determined parameters, including a blade radius of 2 m, a tip speed ratio (λ) of 7, a pitch angle (ß) of 0 degree, and an air density of 1.225 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, The output may help in solving Kupang's electricity issues and reach 23% of renewable energy target by 2025.

articleTitle: A Smart Demand-Side Management Framework for Residential Communities with Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The growing adoption of electric vehicles (EV s) in the automotive sector offers significant opportunities to transform the power industry. The full potential of EV s can be harnessed to improve grid operations, optimize energy management, and reduce energy costs. This paper proposes a Smart Demand-Side Management (SDM) framework for residential communities with EVs to 1) reduce the charging cost in a Real-Time Pricing (RTP) tariff environment, 2) obtain more Demand Response (DR) incentives without sacrificing the comfort, and 3) fairly allocate the community charging infrastructure. The former two operates at individual residences level and the last one suitable for community level management. In all these cases, by leveraging Vehicle- To-Grid (V2G) technology, the system enables EV s to discharge power back to the grid during high-demand periods, effectively managing peak-load hours and providing users with cost-saving opportunities. The proposed SDM framework is tested on MATLAB programming platform with linprog solver for various test cases and found to be significantly effective for all three objectives.

articleTitle: Fatigue-Reduction Active Power Allocation in Wind Farms Using Convex Reward Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: As global emphasis shifts toward renewable energy, particularly wind power, ensuring the reliability and safety of wind turbines has become imperative, especially given the significant costs associated with maintenance. This paper presents a novel approach to minimizing equivalent fatigue loads in wind farms through a Fatigue-Reduction active power allocation algorithm that leverages convex reward reinforcement learning. The proposed algorithm integrates Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning with Input Convex Neural Networks (ICNN) to enhance convergence and generalization while effectively addressing the nonlinear dynamics inherent in wind farm operations. A sliding window equivalent fatigue load calculation model based on ICNN is introduced, transforming the fatigue assessment problem into a convex optimization framework, thereby improving computational efficiency. The study employs a 50MW wind farm simulation to evaluate the proposed methods, demonstrating superior performance in fatigue load reduction compared to traditional approaches. The results indicate substantial improvements in both computational speed and accuracy, underscoring the practical applicability of this methodology for optimizing wind farm operations.

articleTitle: Optimization of Battery Energy Storage Systems for Energy Markets and Future Energy Communities
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The increasing integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) into electrical grids presents also challenges related to grid stability and market dynamics. Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) have emerged as a potential solution to these challenges, offering capabilities for energy storage and support services that enhance grid reliability. This paper explores the optimization of the operations of such components with a case study in the Italian electricity market context. The research employs a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model to optimize the participation of BESS in the Day-ahead market, under the specific regulatory framework of a stock martket tender. By analyzing historical data and simulating BESS operations, this study identifies proper strategies to maximize economic returns and enhance the competitive positioning of storage systems in a specific European market context.

articleTitle: Estimating the Global, Beam and Diffuse Components of Photosynthetically Active Radiation Using Physically Constrained Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Surface photosynthetically active radiation (PAR; 400–700 nm) components—global horizontal, beam normal, and diffuse horizontal—are critical for ecosystem and solar energy applications, particularly in open-field agrivoltaic systems. However, the scarcity of outdoor measurements limits the availability of these data. Machine learning (ML) offers a powerful and practical alternative to traditional parameterization-based methods to modeling the three PAR components. This study develops a physically constrained multi-output neural network based on the multi-gate mixture-of-experts (MMoE) architecture to simultaneously estimate the three PAR components. A specially designed constraint layer ensures adherence to the fundamental physical relationship (i.e., the closure equation). Compared to several single-output semi-empirical and ML models, the proposed model demonstrates superior performance on the test set, with average normalized root mean square error (nRMSE), normalized mean absolute error (nMAE), normalized mean bias error (nMBE), and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values of 4.1997%, 2.8888%, -0.9775%, and 0.9975, respectively. Notably, the model's outputs perfectly satisfy the physical constraint, achieving zero relevant errors, whereas other ML models exhibit varying degrees of errors, with their maximum values ranging from 1% to 3%.

articleTitle: A Method and Device for Renting Services and Transferring Property Rights to a Quality Power Supply Operation
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: In order to reduce the power quality governance cost and investment risk for users, this paper proposes a method and device for high-quality power supply operation with rental services and property rights transfer.
