By grouping and governing user-sensitive equipment, the capacity of voltage governance equipment that can be directly purchased or selected for leasing is screened out. And thereby an expense optimization model is established to ultimately achieve the goal of maximizing the total net income of sensitive users and governance equipment manufacturers. Taking a sensitive user and equipment supplier as an example, a calculation example analysis is carried out. The results show that the method proposed in this paper can achieve the effect of maximizing the benefits of users and equipment manufacturers.

articleTitle: A Study of Travel Patterns in Electric Taxis, Private Vehicles, and Private Hire Vehicles in Singapore
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)

authors.preferredName: Siti Nur Nadzirah Binti Mohamed Sani

abstract: Electric vehicles (EV s) are gaining popularity as a greener alternative to conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles in several nations, including Singapore. With the goal of electrifying all vehicles by 2040, Singapore aims to significantly reduce emissions from its transportation sector. However, the large-scale integration of EV s will have substantial implications for the electrical grid. This thesis investigates the potential of different vehicle types for grid integration and services through a comparative analysis of travel patterns among conventional taxis, private vehicles, and private hire vehicles in Singapore. An online survey, administered via Qualtrics, was used to collect detailed travel data from a representative sample of drivers. The analysis reveals distinct driving patterns across the three vehicle categories. Based on daily driving distances, departure and arrival times, and parking locations, this study evaluates the additional load demand and identifies trends in EV availability for grid operations. The findings indicate that private vehicles exhibit greater availability for grid services when parked outside the home, compared to private hire vehicles and taxis. This study provides critical insights into identifying the most suitable vehicle types for grid integration and highlights their potential role in supporting a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: The Structural Optimization Design and Temperature Uniformity Promotion of Battery Energy Storage Station Using Liquid-Air Combined Cooling Method
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: Thermal management of liquid-cooled battery energy storage stations (BESSs) is becoming a hot research topic. At present, a liquid cooling plate in the heat management system is primarily located at the bottom of batteries. However, The battery temperature uniformity deteriorates owing to the poor heat transfer at the battery bottom, which affects the service life of the battery. Thus, this study proposes a battery liquid flow inter-wall heat transfer structure by CFD modeling. Under the 2P frequency modulation condition, the results of simulation showed that the maximum temperatures difference and average temperature of the battery cluster were 6.5 and 300.8 K at the end of the discharge period, respectively. In order to further improve the uniformity of temperature distribution in the battery cluster system, a liquid-air combined thermal management system was designed based on the battery liquid flow inter-wall heat transfer structure. Four kinds of liquid-air structures a, b, c and d are proposed. In the optimal structure d, at the end of the discharge period, the maximum temperature difference of the battery cluster was 1.3 K, which exhibited an effective improvement of 80.2% compared with that of the liquid flow inter-wall heat transfer structure. The proposed liquid-air combined thermal management system effectively restrains the unacceptable heat transfer at the heat transfer terminal and deterioration of single battery temperature; in addition, it can extend the battery cycle life and helps improve the use economy of BESSs.

articleTitle: Incorporation of Optimal Energy Storage Systems and CCUS Project into Power Market Trading
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: To achieve carbon neutrality in integrated energy system (IES), installing energy storage systems (ESSs) and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) technology are crucial. Establishing a future low-carbon electricity structure is gaining increasing attention. This paper first explored the potential of short-term and long-term energy storage through optimization method of minimum carbon emission, as well as the analysis feasibility of CCUS deployment. Based on the optimized energy structure, different power generation types will participate in the electricity market trading, modified Shapley value method are proposed to enhance to increase the profits of renewable energy and low-carbon power generation. Finally, taking Inner Mongolia, China as a case study, exploring the benefits and carbon emission of the optimized energy structure participated in the electricity trading market. According to the case analysis, taking the 2030 low-carbon plan as an example, the optimized ESSs can reduce carbon emissions about 15%, although it may experience short-term losses. The CCUS deployment in thermal power generation can accelerate carbon reduction more effectively. The improved profit allocation method effectively promotes the profitability of renewable energy and low-carbon power generation in the electricity market, increasing solar, wind, and CCUS profits by 3%, 5%, and 2%, respectively.

articleTitle: Optimization Algorithm-Based Biofuel Blending Scheme and Its Stability Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: The blending ratio of marine fuel is closely related to both cost and quality, and biofuels face similar challenges. To develop a more effective blending scheme and address issues such as significant quality margins and the potential for unqualified products that may require adjustments during manual formulation based on experience, an optimization algorithm was used on the biofuel blending scheme calculation. The objective function focused on minimizing costs, while quality conditions served as constraints. The optimized formulation for the blending schemes were calculated. Compatibility was assessed through spot tests, revealing that the blended products received Class I or II. However, stability issues emerged when large quantities of biodiesel were added to a blend of hydrogenated residue and desolidified slurry, leading to delamination during prolonged storage. The inclusion of specific light diesel fuels can mitigate the deterioration rate of the blended fuel and enhance stability. By employing the gradient property method for scheme verification and comparing results from long period and rapid stability tests, it was found that the B20 exhibited superior stability. Furthermore, the rapid stability of the six schemes aligned with the trends observed in long period stability changes, allowing for the prediction of blended biofuel stability during storage and transportation using the rapid stability evaluation method.

articleTitle: Design of a Darrieus-Savonius Wind Turbine Incorporating Rotary and Linear Generating Systems Using Scotch Yoke Mechanism with IoT Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 9th International Conference on Green Energy and Applications (ICGEA)
abstract: This study presents the design of a Darrieus-Savonius wind turbine integrated with rotary-linear generator. The system combines the aerodynamic upgrades of the Darrieus rotor with the self-starting capability of the Savonius rotor, coupled with a rotary-linear generator to enhance power generation. Both the rotary and linear generators use a gear train to amplify rotational and linear motion for additional power output. The linear generator incorporates a Scotch -Yoke mechanism, which works alongside the rotary generator. The wind turbine system also features IoT -based wireless monitoring for real-time data acquisition, using INA219 sensors to measure current, voltage, and power, with the Blynk App for remote monitoring. The system was tested under both controlled and uncontrolled wind conditions, and its performance was simulated in MATLAB Simulink for theoretical output prediction. During the uncontrolled test, three setups (morning, noon, and afternoon) were tested, with ANOVA analysis showing significant differences in power generation due to varying wind speeds, especially higher speeds in the afternoon. In the controlled test, the system was tested in a closed environment using an industrial fan simulating wind speeds of 2.4m/s, 3.2m/s, and 3.6m/s. The results indicated significant differences in power output, with system efficiencies of 33.27%,28.42%, and 27.59% for each wind speed, respectively.
